# Tasks & Questions — automatic task teardown, live progress, clarification flow

This document describes the feature added on top of the existing J.A.R.V.I.S.
architecture. Nothing existing was rebuilt: the live dispatcher, the permission
gates, the action ledger, the model-driven `task_plan` tool, the coding-approval
cards and the floating-panel system are all untouched and still do exactly what
they did before.

## What it does

Every **non-greeting user request** now produces one **task record** with:

* a unique id (`TASK-2026-000001`, generated by the existing persisted
  correlation-id source in `observability/diagnostics.py`);
* its own lifecycle `CREATED → INITIALIZING → RUNNING → VALIDATING → COMPLETED`,
  plus `FAILED` and `CANCELLED`;
* an honest checklist — one step per **real tool dispatch** (titled from the
  live activity detail, e.g. `web_search · fusion`), plus the
  analysis/validation/delivery lifecycle stages;
* findings, warnings, errors, artifacts, elapsed time and the user's
  confirmed decisions;
* a structured markdown report at `data/reports/<task_id>.md` once it ends.

A greeting ("hi", "good morning") never creates a record. Off-topic chatter
still gets a lightweight completed record (the spec lists *answering requests*
as a supported operation).

## The honesty contract

* A step completes **only** when the dispatcher classified the real operation
  as `SUCCESS`.
* A permission refusal marks the step **skipped** (nothing ran) and records a
  warning.
* Anything else marks it **failed** and keeps the real error text.
* A step whose work never happened is marked **skipped**, never completed.
* Reports contain real execution data only — no metrics are invented, no
  credentials (every text field is scrubbed with the structured logger's own
  scrubbing), and no model chain-of-thought.

## Clarification questions (when they help, never by default)

A request that already states its approach runs immediately. Questions appear
only when an unresolved choice would materially change the work:

| Trigger | Question | Branches to |
|---|---|---|
| `dev_agent`/`code_helper` write with no approach stated | implementation approach | file scope, but only when it is still open |
| `web_research` that is substantial (or has no depth stated) | research depth | summary |
| `documents` with no format named | document format | summary |

Recommendations are **computed from the request, the skill registry chain, the
named files and previous answers** — never one fixed answer for every question.
The gate holds the **first material tool call** of the task (before anything has
executed), collects the answers, and returns them to the model as
`[USER_DECISIONS]` so it re-plans with those parameters. Cancelling the gate
returns `[CLARIFICATION_CANCELLED]` and marks the task `CANCELLED`; the tool is
never executed.

### §7 limitation (deliberate, documented)

This build does **not** generate questions with a live language model. The Live
session plans internally and exposes no reliable pre-execution question hook, so
questions come from the **deterministic** definitions in
`brain/task_questions.py`. Adding an LLM-assisted generator later means
implementing the same `QuestionDef` contract behind a feature flag; nothing else
changes.

### Answer channels

1. **Task panel** (authoritative) — options, recommended marker + reason, custom
   answer, single/multi-select, Back / Skip / Next, summary + confirm.
2. **Chat card** — `jarvis-answer:<task>:<question>:<option>` anchors, resolved
   by `MarkdownTextBrowser._on_anchor_clicked` into the *same* service.
3. **Voice** — the `question_answer` tool relays a spoken answer, stores the
   user's utterance as evidence, and **never auto-selects** a recommendation.
   The flow always ends on the explicit summary + confirm step.

Optional decisions are never asked at all: the documented default is used and
recorded in the report. A required question waits indefinitely (visible
`waiting` step + Cancel + interrupt), because a recommendation must never be
treated as confirmed just because time passed.

## Where the code lives

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `brain/task_engine.py` | records, lifecycle, checklist steps, event bus, sqlite persistence (`data/runtime/task_records.sqlite`), markdown reports |
| `brain/task_questions.py` | deterministic question definitions, branching sessions, the blocking collection gate, the answer channels |
| `ui_task_panel.py` | `TaskProgressPane` (live checklist, REPORT/CANCEL) and `QuestionFlowView` (the question UI) |
| `main.py` | per-turn task creation, the dispatcher gate, step/result reporting, `question_answer` tool, turn settlement, question-service binding |
| `ui.py` | two signals, the `tasks` floating panel, chat cards, anchor handling, the `JarvisUI` facade methods |

Threading: tool calls run on the Live session's asyncio loop, so the gate
collects through `loop.run_in_executor(...)` and the loop keeps servicing audio.
All widget updates go through Qt signals emitted from the worker thread.

## Feature flags (`config/settings.py`)

| Flag | Default | Effect when off |
|---|---|---|
| `task_teardown` | `True` | no task records are created at all (pre-feature behaviour) |
| `task_questions` | `True` | nothing is asked; every request executes immediately |
| `task_panel_auto_open` | `True` | the panel stays closed until asked for; records still work |

## Using it

* Open the panel: ask J.A.R.V.I.S. to open the **tasks** panel
  (`jarvis_window` accepts `tasks`, `jobs`, `task_progress`, `task_monitor`), or
  let it auto-open when a task starts. `task` still means the web research queue.
* Close the panel from its rail — the task keeps running and its state is kept.
* `REPORT` opens the completed markdown report in the content surface.
* `CANCEL` (only for open tasks) releases any pending question and stops the turn.

## Adding a question definition

1. Write a `QuestionDef` with stable option ids and `recommend_when` predicates
   in `brain/task_questions.py`.
2. Give it a `next_question(ctx)` rule when it should branch.
3. Register the flow in `build_flow(...)` with a strict trigger so it only fires
   when the choice is genuinely unresolved.

Tests to mirror: `tests/unit/test_task_questions.py`,
`tests/unit/test_question_flow.py`, `tests/unit/test_question_gate.py`,
`tests/ui/test_task_panel.py`, `tests/ui/test_task_panel_flow.py`.
